patterns.usage_note: Counterfactual ところ: the event came right to the brink and then did NOT happen, so it is set up by もう少しで, 危[あぶ]なく, あやうく or a counterfactual conditional (〜なければ…するとこだ, 'I would have …'). Do not confuse it with the imminent-action ところ of これから出るところだ (l2 0481), which schedules an event that really is about to occur: the same 辞書形＋ところ shape, opposite outcome, and only this near-miss reading takes もう少しで／危なく. Keep the plain だ here; the explicitly past 〜ところだった is catalogued as its own pattern (l2 2091), and after the past tense 〜たところ the noun instead means 'had just done it'. とこ is the clipped conversational shape.

examples.ruby: もう少[すこ]しで電車[でんしゃ]に乗[の]り遅[おく]れるとこだ。
examples.english: I came within a hair of missing my train.

examples.ruby: 君[きみ]が思[おも]い出[だ]させてくれなければ、約束[やくそく]をすっぽかすとこだ。
examples.english: If you hadn't reminded me, I'd have blown off the appointment.

examples.ruby: 一歩[いっぽ]間違[まちが]えば大[おお]けがをするところだ。
examples.english: One wrong step and you'd be badly hurt.
